workEn: The Secret History of the Mongols
title: 元朝秘史 §§154–157
titleEn: The Secret History of the Mongols — §§154–157: The Tatars Destroyed, Yesügen and Yesui, and Wang Qan's Raid
part: §§154–157 — The Tatars Destroyed, Yesügen and Yesui, and Wang Qan's Raid
source: Mongγol-un niγuča tobčiyan (The Secret History of the Mongols), §§154–157, in the Ming Chinese-character phonetic transcription, as edited with a romanized reading by Shiratori Kurakichi 白鳥庫吉, 音訳蒙文元朝秘史 (Tokyo, 1943), itself based on the Ye Dehui 葉德輝 printed edition of 1905/1908; text taken from the Japanese Wikisource transcription, archived and verified against it character for character. Shiratori died in 1942, so the edition was public domain in Japan before the URAA date and was never restored in the United States. Section numbering (§) is the standard citation system. Romanization convention: Shiratori's, kept exactly as he prints it (γ, ġ, ṅ, ž, č, and the raised dot of γ̇). Translations are made fresh from the Mongolian, with the Ming interlinear Chinese glosses as the primary crib. No modern translation was consulted. langCode is null: there is no text-to-speech for Middle Mongol.
about: Four sections. §154: after the Tatars have been broken, Chinggis Qahan takes counsel alone with his kin in a tent and proposes to measure the Tatars against a cart's linchpin, destroy them and make slaves of the remnant; Belgütei, asked by Jeke-Chelen what was said, lets it out, the Tatars fortify, and the army suffers badly in the assault, so Chinggis bars Belgütei from the great council. §155: Yesügen Qatun, the daughter of a Tatar, is taken by Chinggis, tells him that her elder sister Yesui was fit for a qan, and the sister is found and seated in Yesügen's own place, with Yesügen below her. §156: at a feast Yesui sighs, Chinggis has the assembled people stand tribe by tribe, and a young stranger who stands apart is questioned and beheaded. §157: a short report of Wang Qan's raid on the Merkid in the Dog year, which ends with Chinggis given nothing. The councils of §154 and the two women's speeches in §155 lean heavily on the Ming glosses, and a number of readings are marked as first readings in the notes.
draftNote: The Mongol readings follow Shiratori throughout; the English is a first drafting.

sentences.t: Tatar-i muqudγažu daγ̇ulin baražu ulus irgen an-u ker kikün keġen

morph.gloss: to wipe out, destroy (stem inferred from the Ming 絕 'cut off') [敎絕着]
to be finished, used up, ruined [了着]
people, the common folk of a camp or realm [百姓]
their (third-person genitive, back-vowel companion of in-ü, set after its noun) [他的]
participle: 'that which will be done' (with ker, 'how shall we do')

sentences.l: Tatar-ACC wiping-out, plundering, being-finished, realm people, their, how doing-shall, saying,
sentences.i: "Having wiped out and plundered the Tatars and finished them, what shall we do with their realm and people?" — so saying,
sentences.n: The Ming 麽道 (keġen, 'saying') closes a thought that opens the next unit: this is what Chinggis asked. The first three verbs are a converb chain (muqudγažu, daγ̇ulin, baražu: 'wiping out, plundering, finishing'), and I have cut the chain here and left kikün keġen ('shall we do, saying') as its end. muqudγa- is my inference from the Ming 絕 'cut off'; I cannot analyse it further. an-u is 'their', the back-vowel partner of in-ü. kikün is ki- 'to do' with the participle -kün; the Ming writes it 做咱 'let us do'. I take the whole as an indirect question about the people left after the war, which is how the next unit reads.

sentences.t: Čiṅgis Qaγan jeke eje uruk(i)-jar(i)-jan γaγča ger-tür orožu ejetüldübe.

morph.gloss: Chinggis, the title borne by Temüjin from 1206 [太祖︀]

words.reading: 兀舌魯乞-牙舌里-顏 uruk(i)-jar(i)-jan

morph.gloss: kin, kinsfolk (Ming 一族) [一族 自的行]
to take counsel together (eje 'counsel' plus a verbal and reciprocal element, taken as one stem as in the published ejetüldüžü; analysis uncertain) [共商量了]

sentences.l: Čiṅgis Qaγan, great counsel, with-kin-own, alone, house-in entering, took-counsel-together.
sentences.i: Chinggis Qahan went alone into a tent with his own kin and took great counsel.
sentences.n: A plain sentence, verb last. γaγča orožu 'alone entering' is one chain; ger-tür is ger 'house, tent' with the dative-locative -tür ('in', Ming 裏). ejetüldübe is built on eje 'counsel' (the stem is read as in the published ejetüldüžü, with the reciprocal sense of Ming 共商量了 'consulted together') with the past -be. The oddity is uruk(i)-jar(i)-jan (Ming 一族 自的行): uruk 'kin', then -jar, the instrumental 'with' of the published parts (compare jar-an, instrumental plus the reflexive), then the reflexive -(i)jan; the bracketed (i)s are Shiratori's. 'With his own kin' fits the Ming, but the division of the word is a reading.

sentences.t: Ejetüldürün: "Erte üdür-eče Tatar irgen ebüges ečigeš-i baraγsan büleġe.

morph.gloss: to take counsel together (see ejetüldübe) [商量說道]
grandfather, forefather (read from the Ming 祖宗) [祖︀宗]
to be finished, ruined (here transitive: 'to ruin') [廢盡的]

sentences.l: Counselling-together-when: "Formerly from days, Tatar people, ancestors, fathers-ACC having-ruined was.
sentences.i: While they took counsel together he said: "In former days the Tatar people ruined our ancestors and fathers.
sentences.n: A quotation opens at Erte (the opening quotation mark is printed on it). ejetüldürün is the same verb as before with the converb -rün, Ming 商量說道 'saying in counsel'; I take it as the verb of speaking. erte üdür-eče is 'from early days' (ablative -eče). ebüges ečigeš-i are ebüge and ečige with the plural -s, the accusative -i written 行 by the Ming; 'ruined' is baraγsan büleġe, a participle with 'was', i.e. a past perfect (bara- is 'to be finished, ruined'; its use with an object is read from the Ming 廢盡的). 'Our' is not in the Mongol; the next sentence makes it plain that the speakers' own ancestors are meant.

sentences.t: Ebüges ečiges-ün öšül öšüžü kisal kisažu čiγ̇un-dur uližu kidužu alažu öġüje;

morph.gloss: grandfather, forefather (read from the Ming 祖宗) [祖︀宗]
grudge, enmity, a score to settle (Ming 仇; the published kisal has 讎) [仇]
to requite, to settle a score [報着]
linchpin of a cart (Ming 車轄) [車轄 行]
to compare, to measure (Ming 比 'compare') [比着]
to cut off, destroy utterly (Ming 盡絕) [盡絕着]
to give (here after a converb chain, as an auxiliary; Ming 與 'give') [與咱]
hortative: 'let us' (linking vowel ü + -je; Ming 咱 'we')

sentences.l: Ancestors, fathers' vengeance avenging, grudge requiting, linchpin-at comparing, destroying, killing, let-us-give;
sentences.i: Let us avenge the enmity of our ancestors and fathers and requite the grudge: let us measure them against the linchpin, destroy them and kill them.
sentences.n: Two paired objects (öšül and kisal, glossed 讐 and 仇, both 'enmity') each with its verb (öšüžü, kisažu, Ming 報着 'requiting'), then a chain: uližu, kidužu, alažu and the closing öġüje. čiγ̇un is the cart's linchpin (Ming 車轄; čiġü in §§121–124 has the same gloss) and uli- is 'to compare' (Ming 比), so čiγ̇un-dur uližu is 'comparing at / against the linchpin'. What the comparison decides, who is killed and who spared, this passage does not say, and I have not supplied it: the explanation current for the formula is not in the Ming gloss and is left out. The last verb is ög- 'to give' with the hortative -üje (Ming 與咱, 'let us give'); I take it as an auxiliary after the converbs and let 'let us' cover the series, so 'give' is not rendered in the English. That reading of ög- is unsure.

sentences.t: ülidtele kiduja; hülegsed-i boγ̇ollduja žüg žüg qubijalduja"

morph.gloss: to destroy utterly (stem inferred; Ming 盡絕 'cut off utterly'; compare the published ülidgebe) [盡絕]
to cut off, destroy utterly [殺︀着]
verb-maker: 'to make into' (Ming 做使; perhaps the reciprocal -ldu-, uncertain)
to divide, share out (read from the Ming 分) [分咱]

sentences.l: Until-destroyed killing-let-us; remnants-ACC slave-making-let-us, direction direction dividing-let-us"
sentences.i: Let us wipe them out down to the last, and let us make slaves of those who remain and share them out in every direction."
sentences.n: The quotation ends at qubijalduja" (closing mark). ülidtele is ülid- 'to destroy' (compare ülidgebe in other parts; Ming here 盡絕 'cut off utterly') with -tele 'until', so 'down to the last' is my reading of the Ming. hülegsed-i 'those who remained' (past participle, plural -d, accusative -i; Ming 剩的(每)行) is the object of boγ̇ollduja, boγ̇ol 'slave' with -ldu-, a verb-maker I read from the Ming 做使 'make' (perhaps the reciprocal), and -ja 'let us' (Ming 奴婢做使咱). qubijalduja is qubi- 'to share' with the reciprocal -jaldu- (as in the published entry) and -ja (Ming 分咱); žüg žüg is 'each quarter' (Ming 各 處). Three -ja 'let us' verbs in a row are the whole proposal.

sentences.t: keġen eje baraldužu, ger- tēče γaruγ̇asu Tatar-un Jeke-Čelen Belgütei-eče ambar eje ejetüldübe" keġen asaγčuγ̇u.

house, tent (printed with a hyphen; the ending -eče follows on the next word) [房子]
ablative: from (written with a long vowel, as in -dēče; Ming 行 where one expects 處) [行]
conditional: 'if, when' (the u a linking vowel after a consonant; Ming 呵)
Jeke-Chelen, a man's name (Ming 人名) [人名]
Belgütei, a man's name (Ming 人名) [人名 處]

past tense: 'had -ed' (the form of -žuγ̇u after a consonant stem; Ming 有來)

sentences.l: Saying, counsel settled-having, house from going-out-when, Tatar's Jeke-Čelen, Belgütei-from, "what-sort counsel took-counsel-together" saying, had-asked.
sentences.i: Having so settled the counsel, as they went out of the tent, Jeke-Chelen of the Tatars asked Belgütei, "What counsel have you taken together?"
sentences.n: keġen again closes the quotation. baraldužu is baraldu- 'to settle together' (Ming 定了着). The word ger- is printed with a hyphen and its ablative tēče (Ming 行) stands on the next line; I join them as 'from the house' (-tēče is the ablative written with a long vowel, as -dēče elsewhere). γaruγ̇asu is γar- 'to go out' with -uγ̇asu 'when' (a linking u, then -γ̇asu; Ming 呵). Shiratori puts no stop between this clause and the next, so the two stand in one unit. Jeke-Čelen is a man of the Tatars (Tatar-un, genitive) and the ablative -eče on Belgütei means 'from Belgütei', so 'asked of'. ambar eje is Ming 怎生商量 'what counsel'; ejetüldübe is the earlier verb, and the quotation marks open and close on the Ming's own line. asaγčuγ̇u is asaγ- 'to ask' with -čuγ̇u, the past that is -žuγ̇u after a consonant (Ming 問了有來, 'had asked'). Why a Tatar should be at hand to ask is not said, and I do not guess.

sentences.t: Belgütei ügülerün: "Tan-i bügüde-ji čiγ̇un-dur uližu kiduja keġeldübe" keġežüġü.

morph.gloss: linchpin of a cart [車轄 行]
to destroy utterly (Ming 盡殺) [盡殺︀]

sentences.l: Belgütei speaking-when: "You-ACC all-ACC linchpin-at comparing, destroying-let-us, we-said" said.
sentences.i: Belgütei, speaking, said: "We have said together: let us measure all of you against the linchpin and kill you."
sentences.n: Belgütei answers by repeating the plan. Tan-i is the second-person plural 'you' with the accusative (Ming 您行) and bügüde-ji 'all' (accusative): 'you, all of you'. The verb is kiduja, hortative ('let us kill'). keġeldübe is keġe- 'to say' with the reciprocal -ldü- and the past -be, i.e. 'we said together, we agreed' (Ming 共說了). keġežüġü ends the sentence ('he said'), as in Ming 說有來. So Belgütei is passing the secret on in a few words. Whether he meant it as a warning or was careless is not stated.

sentences.t: Belgütei-jin ene üge-dür Jeke-Čelen Tatar-tur-(i)-jan tuṅqaγ talbižu qorγaγlažuγ̇u.

morph.gloss: Tatar, the Tatars [種(名) 自的行]
notice, proclamation, word sent (Ming 傳說) [傳說]
to put, to set, to let go [放着]

morph.gloss: to fortify, to set up a stockade (Ming 寨子把) [寨子把了來]

sentences.l: Belgütei's this word-in, Jeke-Čelen, own-Tatars-to, notice sending-out, had-fortified.
sentences.i: Because of these words of Belgütei, Jeke-Chelen sent word to his own Tatars, and they fortified themselves.
sentences.n: Belgütei-jin takes the genitive -jin after a vowel, and ene üge-dür is 'in this word', so 'by these words'. tuṅqaγ talbižu is 'putting out a notice' (Ming 傳說 'to pass word'; talbi- 'to put, to let go'); Tatar-tur-(i)-jan is 'to his own Tatars', dative-locative -tur plus the reflexive. The main verb is qorγaγlažuγ̇u, from qorγaγla- 'to make a stockade' (Ming 寨子把 'to hold a fort'), past -žuγ̇u. Who 'they' are is the Tatars, though the Mongol has no plural marker and the subject could be only Jeke-Chelen himself.

sentences.t: Qorγalaγsad Tatar-tur bidan-u čeriġüd eġerekün bolun maši samšižuγ̇u.

words.reading: 中豁舌兒中合中剌黑撒惕 Qorγalaγsad

glyphs.s: 中豁舌兒中合中剌黑撒惕

morph.gloss: to fortify (the stem qorγala- here, qorγaγla- in qorγaγlažuγ̇u) [寨子把了的(每)]
plural past participle: 'those who had fortified'

converb: -ing (the Ming 呵 makes it 'if, when')

sentences.l: The-fortifiers, Tatars-to, our soldiers attacking-about-to being, very ruined.
sentences.i: When our army was about to attack the Tatars who had fortified, it was badly ruined.
sentences.n: Qorγalaγsad is a plural participle, 'those who had fortified', and the Ming 寨子把了的(每) says the same. Tatar-tur 'to the Tatars' is a dative of direction (Ming 行). bidan-u čeriġüd is 'our soldiers' (čeri 'soldier' plus the plural -ġüd, Ming 軍每). eġerekün bolun is 'about to attack' (-kün participle, bolun a converb, Ming 做呵). The verb is samšižuγ̇u, 'wasted, ruined' (Ming 廢耗了); I put 'badly ruined' for maši samšižuγ̇u and take it to mean heavy losses. The grammar of the first words (the fortifiers as a kind of topic) is loose, and I have smoothed it.

sentences.t: Qorγalaγ- sad Tatar-i žobožü oroγ̇ulžu ülüdgen čiγ̇un-dur uližu kiduqui-dur

words.reading: 中豁舌兒中合剌黑- Qorγalaγ-

morph.gloss: to fortify (printed qorγalaγ- with the participle's γ; the plural -sad follows on the next line; also written qorγaγla-) [寨子把了的]
to toil, to suffer (Ming 生受) [生受着]
to destroy utterly (variant of ülid-; Ming 盡絕) [盡絕]
linchpin of a cart [車轄 行]

sentences.l: Fortifiers, Tatars-ACC, toiling, making-enter, utterly linchpin-at comparing, destroying-when,
sentences.i: When, after toiling and making (their way) in, they were measuring the fortified Tatars against the linchpin and killing them utterly,
sentences.n: A printed line-break splits Qorγalaγ- from -sad; the join gives the same word as before. žobožü oroγ̇ulžu is 'toiling, causing to enter', Ming 生受着 敎入着 'with effort, making (them) go in'; who is made to go in is not said. ülüdgen is read as 'utterly' from the Ming 盡絕 'cut off' (ülüd- seems to be a variant of ülid- in ülidtele above, with the same gloss; the -ge- is uncertain). kiduqui-dur is kidu- 'to kill off' with the participle -qui and -dur, 'at the killing' (Ming 時, 'when'). The Mongol sentence goes on in the next unit.

sentences.t: Tatar ügüleldürün:" Küġün tutum qančun-dur(i)-jan kituγai qančulažu dere abun üküje" keġeldüžü basa maši-kü samšižuγ̇u.

morph.gloss: sleeve (Ming 袖) [袖 裏自的行]
to put in the sleeve, to tuck away (Ming 袖着) [袖着]
cushion, back-pad (the Ming here has 藉背 'rest on the back'; the same word is glossed 墊背 elsewhere, where it suggests a companion taken along in death) [藉背]
to ruin, to waste [廢耗有來]

sentences.l: Tatars speaking-together-when: "Man each, sleeve-in-own, knife in-the-sleeve-putting, cushion taking, let-us-die" saying-together, again very-indeed ruined.
sentences.i: the Tatars, speaking together, said: "Let each man put a knife in his own sleeve, take a back-cushion, and die," and, saying this together, again there were very heavy losses.
sentences.n: The doubtful phrase is dere abun üküje. dere is 'cushion, back-pad' (the published parts have it so, glossed 墊背; here the Ming has 藉背 'rest on the back'); abun is ab- 'to take' with the converb -n, and üküje is ükü- 'to die' with -je 'let us' (Ming 死咱). So 'taking a back-cushion, let us die'; I read the cushion as an enemy taken along in death, an idiom that I infer from the Ming and cannot prove from the grammar. qančun-dur(i)-jan is 'in one's own sleeve' (Ming 袖 裏自的行). ügüleldürün and keġeldüžü are reciprocal forms ('said among themselves'). The sentence ends at samšižuγ̇u, 'ruined' (maši-kü, 'very, indeed'; -kü is the emphatic); the Mongol gives no subject and, as in the earlier samšižuγ̇u, I take it to be our army, whence the neutral 'there were losses'. I end the unit at Shiratori's full stop.

sentences.t: Tedüi Tatar-i čiγ̇un-dur uližu kidun baražu tende Čiṅgis Qaγan žarliγ bolurun;

morph.gloss: so much, so many, thus [那些]
linchpin of a cart [車轄 行]
to be finished, to finish [殺︀了着]
Chinggis, the title borne by Temüjin from 1206 [太祖︀]

sentences.l: So-many Tatars-ACC linchpin-at comparing, destroying, finishing, there Čiṅgis Qaγan decree being-when:
sentences.i: Having measured those Tatars against the linchpin, destroyed them and made an end of them, Chinggis Qahan then issued this decree:
sentences.n: tedüi is 'so many', here before Tatar-i in the sense 'those (Tatars)' (Ming 那些). The converbs kidun baražu 'destroying, finishing' hang from the decree clause; Shiratori has no stop here. tende 'there' is also 'then'. bolurun is bol- 'to be, to become' with the converb -urun (Ming 說道, 'saying'), the formula 'when a decree was made'.

巴舌剌勒都︀黑撒泥 baralduγsan-i

morph.gloss: to settle together, agree [了了的 行]
Belgütei, a man's name [人名 的]
to tell, to report, to declare (Ming 吿) [吿的]

to ruin, to waste, to be spent (Ming 廢耗) [廢耗了]

sentences.l: "We, with-kin-own great counsel finished-ACC, Belgütei's telling because-of, our soldiers very ruined.
sentences.i: "Because Belgütei told what we had settled in our great counsel among our own kin, our army has been badly ruined.
sentences.n: A passage whose logic is clear but whose grammar is not. baralduγsan-i is a past participle 'what was settled together' with an accusative (Ming 了了的 行); žaγ̇aqu-jin tula is 'because of the telling', participle -qu with genitive -jin and the postposition tula (Ming 上頭). The Ming gives samšijaba as 廢耗了 'ruined', and it parallels the earlier samšižuγ̇u (the ending -jaba is uncertain). I take 'bidan-u čeriġüd samšijaba' as the result. Whether the whole was meant as a rebuke to Belgütei or as a ground for the exclusion that follows is the reader's reading; the rule is stated in the next unit.

sentences.t: Eġün-ü qoina jeke eje-dür Belgütei bu orotuγai.

morph.gloss: do not (prohibitive particle; Ming 休) [休]

sentences.l: This-of after, great counsel-in, Belgütei not enter-let.
sentences.i: After this Belgütei is not to enter the great council.
sentences.n: eġün-ü qoina is 'after this' (genitive of eġün 'this', Ming 這的後). bu is the prohibitive, with the optative -tuγai on orotuγai 'let (him) enter' (Ming 者). So 'Belgütei: do not let him enter'. The structure is that of a decree: subject, then verb in the jussive.

sentences.t: Eje baratala γadana bükün-i žasa- tuγai;

morph.gloss: to put in order, to regulate, to punish (Ming 整治) [整治]

sentences.l: Counsel finishing-while, outside being-ACC, ordering-let;
sentences.i: While the counsel is going on, let those who are outside be kept in order;
sentences.n: baratala is bara- 'to be finished' with -tala 'until, while'; the Ming 了間 gives 'in the time of finishing'. bükün-i is 'those who are', the participle of bü- 'to be' (the -kün ending as in kikün) with the accusative. žasa- (Ming 整治) means 'to put in order, to regulate, to punish'; I put 'kept in order', and the next unit goes on to the punishment of offenders.

morph.gloss: to put in order, to regulate [整治了]
quarrel, brawl (Ming 鬭毆) [鬭毆的行]
work, business (Ming 勾當) [勾當有的每 行]

morph.gloss: to judge, to decide a case [敎斷者︀]
optative/jussive: 'let (them) be -' (Ming 敎斷者 'have them judged')

sentences.l: Ordering-having, brawlers, thief, liars, those-doing-business-ACC, let-judge.
sentences.i: and, having put them in order, let brawlers, thieves, liars and men with business on hand be judged.
sentences.n: A list of four offences and one verb. Only kereġür-i and üileten-i take the case ending; qulaγai and qudal are bare nouns (Ming 盜, 謊); 'thieves' and 'liars' are my reading of them. üileten-i is üile 'work, business' with -ten 'having' (Ming 勾當有的每 行), i.e. 'those who have business on hand'; the Ming word 勾當 is 'affair', and in a list of offenders it may carry a sense of wrongdoing, which I do not claim. žasaγ̇ad is 'having put in order', an active converb (Ming 整治了): the subject is those appointed, not the outsiders. žarγulatuγai is žarγu- 'to judge' with a verbal -la- and -tuγai (Ming 敎斷者, 'let (them) be made to judge').

sentences.t: Eje baraγ̇asu ötög ūγsan-u qoina Belgütei, Daγ̇aritai qojar tende orotuγai." keġen žarliγ bolba.

morph.gloss: drinking, a drink offered (Ming 進酒) [進酒]
Da'aritai, a man's name (Ming 人名) [人名]

sentences.l: Counsel finished-when, drinking, those-drank-of after, Belgütei, Daγ̇aritai, two, there enter-let" saying, decree made.
sentences.i: When the counsel is over, after the drinking, let Belgütei and Da'aritai, the two of them, come in." So the decree was made.
sentences.n: baraγ̇asu is bara- with -γ̇asu 'when' (Ming 了呵). ötög ūγsan-u qoina is 'the drink, after having drunk it': ötög (Ming 進酒) with the past participle ūγsan (Ming 飮了的) in the genitive and qoina 'after'. qojar is the numeral for pairs of persons. Daγ̇aritai is a man's name (Ming 人名), of whom nothing else is known here. The decree closes with keġen žarliγ bolba, 'saying, a decree was made'. This ends §154.

sentences.t: Tende Tatar-un Jeke-Čeren-ü ökin Jesügen Qatun-i Čiṅgis Qaγan tende abba.

morph.gloss: Jeke-Cheren, a man's name (Ming 人名; printed Čeren here, Čelen above) [人名 的]
Yesügen, a woman's name (Ming 女名) [女名]
lady, queen, wife of a qan [娘子行]
Chinggis, the title borne by Temüjin from 1206 [太祖︀]

sentences.l: There, Tatar's Jeke-Čeren's daughter, Jesügen Qatun-ACC, Čiṅgis Qaγan there took.
sentences.i: Then Chinggis Qahan took Yesügen Qatun, the daughter of the Tatar Jeke-Cheren.
sentences.n: The § opens with Tende 'there, then'. Jeke-Čeren-ü is a Tatar name (printed Čeren here, Čelen in §154; the Han differ by the 舌 that writes r); I take it to be the Jeke-Čelen who was asked in §154, since the Ming has 人名 for both and both are Tatars, but the text does not prove it. ökin is 'daughter' (Ming 女), the genitive chain is Tatar-un Jeke-Čeren-ü ökin 'the Tatar Jeke-Cheren's daughter'. abba is ab- 'to take' with -ba (Ming 要了). Jesügen Qatun-i is a woman's name (Ming 女名) with the accusative on Qatun. The second tende before abba is another 'there', which I pass over.

sentences.t: Taγ̇alaγdarun Jesügen Qatun ügülerün:"

morph.gloss: to favour, to hold dear (Ming 被寵) [被寵的上頭]
lady, queen, wife of a qan [娘子]

sentences.l: Favoured-when, Jesügen Qatun speaking-when:
sentences.i: Being favoured, Yesügen Qatun said:
sentences.n: taγ̇alaγdarun is taγ̇ala- 'to favour' with the passive -γda- and the converb -run; the Ming 被寵的上頭 says 'on account of being favoured'. I put 'being favoured' and leave it unsaid whether the favour came from the Qahan, though the sense points to him. ügülerün is the ordinary 'when speaking'.

sentences.t: Qaγan sojurγaγ̇asu nama-ji küġün-e bodo-da bolγažu asaramu;

words.reading: 莎余舌兒中合阿速 sojurγaγ̇asu

morph.gloss: to show favour, bestow a grace (Ming 恩賜) [恩賜呵]
thing, real, actual (Ming 物; reading uncertain) [物行]
to raise up, to foster (Ming 擡擧) [擡擧有]

sentences.l: "Qaγan, if-bestowing, me-ACC person-to, thing-to making, raising-is;
sentences.i: "If the Qahan shows me grace, he makes me somebody among people and raises me up;
sentences.n: The hardest line of the speech. sojurγaγ̇asu is sojurγa- 'to show favour' (Ming 恩賜) with -γ̇asu 'if, when' (Ming 呵); the same word is printed split later in this §. nama-ji is 'me' (accusative, Ming 我行). küġün-e bodo-da bolγažu is 'to a person, to a thing, making'; the Ming 人行 物行 gives nothing more. I read it as 'making me a person, a somebody' and treat bodo as a first reading: it may be a word 'thing' or something else. asaramu is asara- 'to raise, to foster' (Ming 擡擧) with the present -mu. I have kept the sense, not the details; the English keeps the Mongol order, 'making' before 'raising'.

sentences.t: nadāča egeči Jesüi neretei nadāča deġere qān küġün-e žokiqui ažiγ̇ai že.

morph.gloss: ablative with long vowel: than (Ming 比 'than')
ablative with long vowel: than (Ming 比 'than')
qan, sovereign (the Ming 皇帝) [皇帝]
emphatic particle at the end of a statement (Ming 也者) [也者︀]

sentences.l: Than-me, elder-sister Jesüi named, than-me higher, qan person-to, fitting was, indeed.
sentences.i: My elder sister, named Yesui, stands above me, and was fit for a qan.
sentences.n: nadāča is 'than me' (the ablative -dāča with a long vowel; Ming 比我), and it comes twice: 'older than me' is the elder sister's place, and deġere, 'above' (Ming 高), is the second comparison; I do not say in what she is higher (rank, age or worth). neretei is nere 'name' with -tei 'having', so 'named' (Ming 名字有的). qān küġün-e žokiqui ažiγ̇ai is 'for a qan-person, fitting, there was' (Ming 皇帝人行合宜的有來): a modest speech, 'she was the fitting one'. že is a sentence-final particle. ažiγ̇ai is a past 'was' whose form I cannot confirm.

sentences.t: Sai küregen küregelen büligi.

morph.gloss: just now, only just (Ming 恰纔) [恰纔]
to take as son-in-law, to be a son-in-law (Ming 做女壻) [做女壻]

sentences.l: Just-now son-in-law, son-in-law-making, was.
sentences.i: She had only just taken a husband.
sentences.n: sai is 'just now' (Ming 恰纔). küregen is 'son-in-law, bridegroom' and küregelen is a verb from it with the converb -n (Ming 做女壻). Literally 'just now, being a son-in-law, was': her sister had lately married. The Ming gives no more, so 'taken a husband' is my reading.

sentences.t: Edöġe maqa ene bodulγan-dur qaγ̇aγši jorčibi" keġebi.

morph.gloss: unknown, who knows (Ming 不知) [不知]

words.reading: 孛都︀勒中罕-突︀舌兒 bodulγan-dur

morph.gloss: turmoil, upheaval (Ming 亂離) [亂離 裏]
past tense: -ed (a variant of -ba/-be, not a first-person ending; Ming 了)
past tense: -ed (a variant of -ba/-be, not a first-person ending; Ming 了)

sentences.l: Now who-knows, this turmoil-in, where went" said.
sentences.i: Now, who knows where she has gone in this turmoil?" she said.
sentences.n: maqa 'unknown' (Ming 不知) is an adverb 'who knows'. bodulγan 'turmoil, upheaval' (Ming 亂離) with -dur is 'in the upheaval' (the war with the Tatars). qaγ̇aγši is 'where to', jorčibi is jorči- 'to go' with the past -bi (Ming 去了; -bi is the same past as -ba/-be and is used for 'she' elsewhere in this part, as in saγ̇ubi, so it is not a first-person ending). keġebi closes the quotation, 'she said'.

sentences.t: Ene üge-dür Čiṅgis Qaγan ügülerün:

morph.gloss: Chinggis, the title borne by Temüjin from 1206 [太祖︀]

sentences.l: This word-in, Čiṅgis Qaγan speaking-when:
sentences.i: At these words Chinggis Qahan said:
sentences.n: Ordinary frame: ene üge-dür 'in this word', and ügülerün 'when speaking'. Nothing needs flagging here.

sentences.t: "Egeči čin-u čima-dāča sain bögsen böġesü eriġülüje.

morph.gloss: ablative with long vowel: than (Ming 比 'than')

sentences.l: "Elder-sister, your, than-you good, being if, let-us-have-sought.
sentences.i: "If your elder sister was better than you are, let us have her sought.
sentences.n: čin-u is 'your' and čima-dāča 'than you'. bögsen böġesü is the past participle 'having been' with a conditional, 'if she was'. eriġülüje is eri- 'to seek' with the causative -ġül- and the hortative -je: 'let us have (her) sought' (Ming 敎尋咱). The thought is that Chinggis wants to see whether the sister is better, which is his way of taking up her modest remark.

sentences.t: Egeči-jen ireġesü žailažu ögkü-jü či keġebe.

morph.gloss: to hide, to avoid (Ming 躱) [躱着]

sentences.l: Own-elder-sister, if-came, hiding, give-will-? you, said.
sentences.i: If your sister came, would you step aside and give way?" he said.
sentences.n: The speaker is Chinggis, answering her modest remark. Egeči-jen is 'one's own elder sister' with the reflexive -jen. ireġesü is 'if (she) came'. žailažu is 'hiding, avoiding' (Ming 躱着). ögkü-jü is ög- 'to give' with the future participle -kü and an interrogative -jü (Ming 與麽, 'give?'). The Ming gives 'hiding, give?' and no more; I take ög- here as an auxiliary after the converb ('step aside for her', 'yield'), which fits her answer in the next speech, where she says she would žaila- to her sister. That is a reading, not a proven one. či is 'you' and keġebe is 'he said' (the past -be).

sentences.t: Jesügen Qatun ügülerün:

morph.gloss: lady, queen, wife of a qan [娘子]

sentences.l: Jesügen Qatun speaking-when:
sentences.i: Yesügen Qatun said:
sentences.n: Frame, as before.

sentences.t: Qaγan sojur- γaγ̇asu egeči-jen ele üžeġesü egeči-deġen žailasu" keġebe.

morph.gloss: to show favour (its first part; the word is split sojur-/γaγ̇asu) [恩賜]
last syllable of the stem sojurγa- (split from sojur- by the line break) [呵]
emphatic particle: only, but (Ming 但) [但]
reflexive-possessive with dative: 'to one's own' (Ming 自的行)
to hide, to avoid, to step aside (Ming 躱) [躱我]
optative, first person: 'I will' (as in the published ögsü; Ming 我 'I')

sentences.l: "Qaγan, if-bestowing, own-elder-sister, indeed, if-seeing, to-own-elder-sister I-hide" said.
sentences.i: "If the Qahan shows favour, then if I see my sister, I shall step aside for her," she said.
sentences.n: sojur-γaγ̇asu is the same word as above, split by the print. ele is the emphatic 'but, only' (Ming 但). üžeġesü is üže- 'to see' with the conditional (Ming 見呵). žailasu is žaila- 'to hide, to avoid' with -su, which I take to be the first-person optative of the published ögsü, 'I will' (Ming 躱我 'I hide'); I render it as 'step aside for' on the strength of the sense in context and of Chinggis's question, not of the Ming, and mark the reading as probable and not sure. egeči-deġen is 'to one's own sister' with the reflexive -deġen (Ming 姐姐 自的行).

sentences.t: Ene üge-dür Čiṅgis Qaγan žarliγ tuṅqaγ̇ažu eriġülüġsü ögdegsen küregen-lüġe qamtu hoilažu jabuqu-ji bidan-u čeriġüd žolγažuγ̇ui.

morph.gloss: Chinggis, the title borne by Temüjin from 1206 [太祖︀]
to proclaim, to send word (Ming 傅着) [傅着]
verbal: to go into the forest (Ming 林裏)
to go, to travel [行的 行]
stem-final n before a case ending
to meet, to come upon [遇着有來]

sentences.l: This word-in, Čiṅgis Qaγan decree proclaiming, if-having-sought, given son-in-law with, together forest-going, going-ACC, our soldiers met-had.
sentences.i: At these words Chinggis Qahan proclaimed a decree, and when he had her sought, our soldiers came upon her going into the forest together with the son-in-law to whom she had been given.
sentences.n: tuṅqaγ̇ažu 'proclaiming' (Ming 傅着) is from tuṅqaγ 'a notice, a proclamation'. eriġülüġsü is the causative of eri- 'to seek' with a conditional (Ming 敎尋呵), 'when he had (her) sought'. ögdegsen küregen-lüġe is 'together with the son-in-law who had been given' (Ming 與了的 女壻 一同); lüġe is the comitative. hoilažu is hoi 'forest' made into a verb (Ming 林裏). jabuqu-ji is the participle 'going' in the accusative (Ming 行的行): the object of žolγažuγ̇ui 'met, came upon' (Ming 遇着有來). I take the missing object ('her') from the sense. bidan-u čeriġüd 'our soldiers' is the subject. Shiratori puts no stop between the two halves, so they stand in one unit.

sentences.t: Ere in-ü dutaγ̇ažuγ̇u.

morph.gloss: to flee, to run away (Ming 走) [走了有來]

sentences.l: Husband, his, fled.
sentences.i: Her husband got away.
sentences.n: ere is 'husband' or 'man' (Ming 丈夫); in-ü is 'his'. dutaγ̇ažuγ̇u is dutaγ̇a- 'to flee, to run away' with the past -žuγ̇u (Ming 走了有來 'ran off'); the root is a first reading.

sentences.t: Jesüi Qatun-i tende abčiraba.

morph.gloss: lady, queen, wife of a qan [娘子行]

sentences.l: Jesüi Qatun-ACC there brought.
sentences.i: They brought Yesui Qatun there.
sentences.n: abčiraba is ab- 'to take' joined with ire- 'to come': 'take and come', the usual 'to bring' (Ming 將來了). tende is 'there, to him'.

sentences.t: Jesügen Qatun Egeči-jen üže- ġed

morph.gloss: lady, queen, wife of a qan [娘子]

sentences.l: Jesügen Qatun, own-elder-sister, having-seen,
sentences.i: Yesügen Qatun, seeing her sister,
sentences.n: üže- 'to see' is printed apart from its converb -ġed, which I join as 'having seen' (Ming 見了). The first clause of a long sentence continues in the next unit.

sentences.t: urida ügülegsen üge-dür kürün bosču saγ̇uγsan saγ̇urin- dür(i)-jen saγ̇ulžu mün öġesün doro saγ̇ubi.

morph.gloss: seat, place to sit (Ming 位子; printed with a hyphen, the ending -dür follows on the next word) [位子]
the same, that very, also (Ming 他) [他]
past tense: -ed (a variant of -ba/-be, not a first-person ending; Ming 了)

sentences.l: Before spoken word-in arriving, rising, sat-where own-seat-in seating, same own below sat.
sentences.i: as she had said before, rose and seated her sister in the place where she herself had sat, and sat down below her.
sentences.n: I read urida ügülegsen üge-dür kürün as 'in accordance with the word she had said before' (Ming 先前說了的言語裏到着, 'arriving at the word said earlier'); kür- 'to reach' with a converb. bosču is bos- 'to rise'. saγ̇uγsan saγ̇urin-dür(i)-jen is 'in her own seat where she had sat': saγ̇urin 'seat' (Ming 位子) is printed with a hyphen and the ending on the next word. saγ̇ulžu is the causative, 'making sit'. mün öġesün doro saγ̇ubi: 'that very own self, below, sat' (Ming 他自己下坐了). The one unit is long; it is a single sentence in the Mongol and the converb chain is not cut here.

sentences.t: Jesügen Qatun-u üge-dür adali boldažu Čiṅgis Qaγan oin-dur(i)-jan oroγ̇ulžu Jesüi Qatun-i abču žerge-dür saγ̇ulba.

morph.gloss: lady, queen, wife of a qan [娘子的]
Chinggis, the title borne by Temüjin from 1206 [太祖︀]
mind, thought (Ming 情懷) [情懷 自的行]
lady, queen, wife of a qan [娘子行]
rank, row, place in a line (Ming 列位) [列位 裏]

sentences.l: Jesügen Qatun's word-in like being-made, Čiṅgis Qaγan, mind-in-own, making-enter, Jesüi Qatun-ACC taking, rank-in seating.
sentences.i: In keeping with Yesügen Qatun's words, Chinggis Qahan took them into his own mind, took Yesui Qatun and seated her in the ranks (of his wives).
sentences.n: adali boldažu is 'being made like' (Ming 相似被做着, 'being similar'); boldažu is bol- with the passive -da-. I take it as 'being matched with her word', that is, 'in keeping with', and oin-dur(i)-jan oroγ̇ulžu as 'making (them) enter his own mind' (the causative of oro-; Ming 情懷 自的行): he let her words enter his thoughts. The Ming gives the parts, not the idiom, and the rendering is a reading. žerge is 'rank, row' (Ming 列位) and the dative-locative gives 'in the row'. The Mongol does not say 'of wives', but the sense of the preceding story requires it, and Yesui is called Qatun. abču is ab- 'to take' with -ču (Ming 要着). saγ̇ulba is the causative 'made sit' with the past -ba. Shiratori puts no stop between the two halves, so they stand in one unit.

sentences.t: Tatar irgen-i daγ̇ulin baražu nigen üdür Čiṅgis Qaγan γada saγ̇užu undalaldurun

morph.gloss: to be finished, to finish [了着]
Chinggis, the title borne by Temüjin from 1206 [太祖︀]

sentences.l: Tatar people-ACC plundering, finishing, one day, Čiṅgis Qaγan outside sitting, drinking-together-when,
sentences.i: After he had finished plundering the Tatar people, one day Chinggis Qahan was sitting outside, drinking with others,
sentences.n: daγ̇ulin baražu is the same pair as at the start of §154 (Ming 擄了着 'plundered, finished'). irgen-i takes the accusative, Ming 行. nigen üdür is 'one day'. undalaldurun is unda- 'to drink' with a verbal -la-, the reciprocal -ldu- and -run (Ming 共飮時), 'when drinking together'. The sentence continues in the next unit with the circumstance of the drinking.

sentences.t: Jesüi Qatun Jesügen Qatun žirin-ü dunda saγ̇užu undalaldun büküi-dür Jesüi Qatun jekede seġürelbi.

morph.gloss: lady, queen, wife of a qan [娘子]
lady, queen, wife of a qan [娘子]
lady, queen, wife of a qan [娘子]

sentences.l: Jesüi Qatun, Jesügen Qatun, two's between sitting, drinking-together being-when, Jesüi Qatun greatly sighed.
sentences.i: and, sitting between Yesui Qatun and Yesügen Qatun, while they drank together, Yesui Qatun sighed deeply.
sentences.n: žirin-ü dunda is 'between the two' (Ming 兩箇的中間); the subject of saγ̇užu is Chinggis, between the two women. undalaldun is unda-la-ldu- with the converb -n, 'drinking together'; büküi-dür is the participle büküi with -dür, 'at the being, while' (Ming 有時). jekede is the dative-locative of jeke 'great', used as an adverb 'greatly' (Ming 大行). seġürelbi is a verb from seġüre- 'to sigh' (Ming 嘆息了), and its -bi is the past. The text gives no reason for the sigh; I would not guess one.

sentences.t: Tende Čiṅgis Qaγan dotora-γ̇an sedkižü Boγ̇orču Muqali-tan nojad-i urižu ireġülžü ügülerün:

morph.gloss: Chinggis, the title borne by Temüjin from 1206 [太祖︀]
reflexive-possessive: one's own (Ming 內 自的行)
Bo'orchu, a man's name (Ming 人名) [(人)名]
Muqali, a man's name (Ming 人名) [人名 等]
and the like, and others (Ming 等)
noyan, lord, commander (Ming 官人) [官人每(行)]

sentences.l: There Čiṅgis Qaγan, inside-own thinking, Boγ̇orču, Muqali-and-others, noyans-ACC summoning, causing-to-come, speaking-when:
sentences.i: Then Chinggis Qahan, turning it over in his mind, summoned Bo'orchu, Muqali and the other noyans, and said:
sentences.n: dotora-γ̇an is 'inside oneself' (Ming 內 自的行), a reflexive; sedkižü is sedki- 'to think'. Muqali-tan has -tan 'and the like' (Ming 等), and nojad-i is nojan 'noyan' (plural -d) in the accusative. urižu is uri- 'to call' and ireġülžü is ire- 'to come' made causative (Ming 敎來着), so 'calling, making come'; the two are a pair, translated as 'summoned'. The unit is a chain of four converbs (sedkižü, urižu, ireġülžü, ügülerün), the last of them 'when speaking'.

sentences.t: "Ta ede ele čiγ̇uluγsad haran büġüdeġer aimaγ aimaγ baidqun;

morph.gloss: emphatic particle: indeed, only (Ming 但) [但]
to assemble, to gather [聚會的(每)]
plural past participle: 'those assembled' (Ming 聚會的每)
all together, all of them (Ming 都) [都︀]
to stand, to be placed [立您]
imperative, second person plural (Ming 您 'you'; compare ügüdkün)

sentences.l: "You, these indeed assembled commoners, all, tribe by tribe, stand;
sentences.i: "All of you who are gathered here, stand tribe by tribe;
sentences.n: Ta is 'you' (plural, Ming 您). ede ele čiγ̇uluγsad haran is 'these, indeed, assembled commoners' (Ming 這的每 但 聚會的每 人). čiγ̇uluγsad is the plural participle of čiγ̇ul- 'to assemble'. büġüdeġer 'all together' (Ming 都) is an adverb. aimaγ aimaγ is repeated (Ming 部落 部落) and means 'tribe by tribe'. baidqun is bai- 'to stand' with -dqun, an imperative for 'you' plural (Ming 立您 'stand, you'; compare ügüdkün elsewhere); the division of the ending is uncertain, the sense is not.

sentences.t: öġer-eče busu aimaγ-un küġün-i öġere böldeidgedkün" keġen žarliγ bolba.

morph.gloss: oneself, one's own (Ming 自巳 'self') [自巳裏]

words.reading: 孛勒迭亦惕客惕坤 böldeidgedkün

morph.gloss: to be solitary, forlorn (stem inferred from the Ming 孤零) [敎孤零您]

sentences.l: from-own, other tribe's person-ACC apart, make-solitary" saying, decree made.
sentences.i: and set apart, alone, any man of a tribe other than your own." So he decreed.
sentences.n: öġer-eče busu is 'other than oneself' (Ming 自巳裏 別): öġer is 'self, one's own'. aimaγ-un küġün-i 'a man of a tribe' (genitive and accusative). öġere is 'apart' (Ming 𠮠, an Extension B character). böldeidgedkün is built on a stem böldeid- that I infer from the Ming 孤零 'solitary, forlorn', with -ge- (causative, Ming 敎) and -dkün, the imperative for 'you' plural (Ming 您): 'make (him) stand alone, you'. The form is uncertain and the sense comes mainly from the Ming. keġen žarliγ bolba closes the speech, 'saying, a decree was made'.

sentences.t: Tedüi aimaγ aimak(i)-jar(i)-jan baiγ̇asu nigen žalaγ̇ui sain gürümele küġün aimaγ̇ud-ača öġre baiba.

words.reading: 阿亦馬乞-牙舌里-顏 aimak(i)-jar(i)-jan

morph.gloss: to stand, to be placed [立呵]
to stand, to be placed [立了]

sentences.l: So-much tribe, tribe-with-own, stood-when, one young good slender man, from-the-tribes apart stood.
sentences.i: When the tribes had so stood, each by itself, one young, fine, slender man stood apart from the tribes.
sentences.n: baiγ̇asu is bai- 'to stand' with the conditional 'when' (Ming 立呵). žalaγ̇ui is 'young' (Ming 年少) and gürümele is 'slender' (Ming 苗條); the Ming picks out his build. aimaγ̇ud-ača is the plural with the ablative, 'from the tribes' (Ming 部落每的 行). The unit has a double reduplication, aimaγ and aimak(i)-jar(i)-jan, which I read as 'tribe by tribe, each in its own'; the -jar is the same doubtful instrumental as before.

sentences.t: "Či jaγ̇un küġün bi" kēġesü
sentences.l: "You what person are?" when-said,
sentences.i: "What man are you?" he was asked,
sentences.n: Či 'you', jaγ̇un 'what' (Ming 甚), küġün 'person'. bi 'is, exists' (Ming 有) closes the quotation. kēġesü is keġe- 'to say' with a conditional, 'if/when (one) said', written with a long vowel (Ming 說呵).

sentences.t: tere küġün ügülerün:
sentences.l: that person speaking-when:
sentences.i: and the man said:
sentences.n: Frame.

sentences.t: "Tatar-un Jeke-Čeren-ü Jesüi neretei ökin ögdegsen küregen küġün büleġe bi.

morph.gloss: Jeke-Cheren, a man's name [人名 的]

sentences.l: "Tatar's Jeke-Čeren's Jesüi named daughter given, son-in-law person was I.
sentences.i: "I was a man, the son-in-law to whom the daughter of the Tatar Jeke-Cheren, named Yesui, had been given.
sentences.n: Here we learn who the stranger is: the husband of Yesui, who had slipped away in §155. Tatar-un Jeke-Čeren-ü Jesüi neretei ökin is 'the daughter named Yesui of Jeke-Cheren of the Tatars' (nere 'name', -tei 'having'). ögdegsen is the passive participle 'given' (Ming 被與的) and belongs to the daughter: the daughter given; küregen is the son-in-law to whom she was given. küġün büleġe bi is 'I was a man'; büleġe is 'was' and bi 'I'. I read this as 'the man who had been given the daughter as wife', i.e. her husband.

sentences.t: Daisun-a daγ̇uliγdarun ajužu buruγ̇udču jabužu edöġe amaurliba že

morph.gloss: to plunder, to carry off [被據時]
to flee, hide, take cover (stem uncertain; Ming 躱) [躱着]
to be at ease, to find peace (Ming 安妥) [安妥了]
emphatic particle at the end of a statement (Ming 也者) [也者︀]

sentences.l: Enemy-by being-plundered-when, fearing, fleeing, going, now peace-found indeed
sentences.i: When I was seized by the enemy I was afraid, and fled, and went about; now I have found peace,
sentences.n: daisun-a daγ̇uliγdarun is 'when seized by the enemy' (daγ̇uli- with the passive -γda- and -run; the dative -a marks the agent, Ming 敵行 被據時). ajužu is aju- 'to fear' (Ming 怕著). buruγ̇udču is buruγ̇ud- 'to flee, hide' (Ming 躱着). amaurliba is 'found ease' (Ming 安妥了). že is the closing particle. The speech goes on in the next unit.

sentences.t: keġen irežü olon haran dotora jaγ̇u tamiγ- daqu keġežü jabulaγ̇a" keġebe

morph.gloss: to recognise, to know a person (stem inferred; Ming 認) [認]
participle: 'what is to be -ed' (the second half of tamiγ-daqu; Ming 的; not the noun daqu 'coat') [的]

sentences.l: saying, coming, many commoners among, whom recognise saying, went-about" said.
sentences.i: So I came, and went about among the many people, not knowing whom to acknowledge," he said.
sentences.n: The words jaγ̇u tamiγ-daqu keġežü are the obscure ones: jaγ̇u 'what, how' (Ming 怎), tamiγ-daqu 'to be recognised', a stem tamiγ- (Ming 認) with the participle -daqu (Ming 的; the token daqu is not the noun 'coat'), keġežü 'saying'. I read 'saying to himself, how or whom shall I recognise', i.e. he was a stranger looking for someone to attach himself to; the Ming does not show whether he was looking for his own people or for new ones. jabulaγ̇a is jabu- 'to go' with a verbal -la- and -γ̇a (Ming 行來 'went about').

sentences.t: Ene üge-ji Čiṅgis Qaγ̇an-a öčiġešü žarliγ bolurun:

morph.gloss: Chinggis, the title borne by Temüjin from 1206 [太祖︀]
to say, to report to a superior (Ming 奏) [奏呵]

sentences.l: This word-ACC Čiṅgis Qaγan-to reporting, decree being-when:
sentences.i: When this was reported to Chinggis Qahan, he decreed:
sentences.n: ene üge-ji is 'this word' with the accusative; Qaγ̇an-a is 'to the Qahan' (Ming 皇帝 行). öčiġešü is a verb of reporting up (Ming 奏呵, 'if/when reported'); the root is not clear to me. žarliγ bolurun is the decree formula, as in §154.

sentences.t: "Mün kü daisu sedkižü oγ̇orčaγ bolžu jabužuγ̇u.

morph.gloss: just, indeed (emphatic particle; Ming 也) [也]
rebellion, revolt (read from the Ming 反 'rebel'; perhaps a form of daisun 'enemy'; uncertain) [反]

sentences.l: "Indeed also rebel thinking, robber being, going-had.
sentences.i: "Indeed, thinking of rebellion, he had been going about as a robber.
sentences.n: mün kü is 'indeed, just so' (Ming 只也). daisu is 'rebellion' (read from the Ming 反 'rebel'; perhaps a form of daisun 'enemy'), a reading, and I take sedkižü to mean 'thinking of'. oγ̇orčaγ is 'robber' (Ming 劫賊). jabužuγ̇u is the past 'had gone, had been going' (Ming 行有來). The Mongol does not say 'he', but a decree about the man is plain.

sentences.t: Edöġe jaγ̇u kürüre irežüġü.

morph.gloss: to spy, to watch for a chance (stem inferred; Ming 窺伺) [窺伺]
converb of purpose: 'in order to -' (as in the published ögüre)

sentences.l: Now what spying, come.
sentences.i: Now what has he come to spy out?
sentences.n: kürüre is kürü- 'to spy, to watch for a chance' (Ming 窺伺) with -re, the converb of purpose seen in ögüre elsewhere, so 'in order to spy'; the stem is inferred. irežüġü is 'has come' (Ming 來有).

sentences.t: In-ü metüs-i čiγ̇un-dur uliba. Jaγ̇u saγ̇aramui;

morph.gloss: like, such as [似他般的每(行)]
linchpin of a cart [車轄 行]
to doubt, to suspect (Ming 疑) [疑]

sentences.l: His likes-ACC linchpin-at compared. What doubting?
sentences.i: Such men as he have been measured against the linchpin. Why doubt?
sentences.n: in-ü metüs-i is 'those like him' (metü 'like', plural -s, accusative; Ming 似他般的每行). čiγ̇un-dur uliba is the formula of §154: 'compared at the linchpin' (Ming 比了). I keep it as 'measured against the linchpin' and do not say what the measuring decided; the next unit shows that the man is put to death, which suggests that being measured was fatal, but that is an inference. saγ̇aramui is saγ̇ara- 'to doubt' with the present -mui (Ming 疑).

sentences.t: nidün-ü ečine gedkün" keġebe.

morph.gloss: behind, at the back (Ming 背處) [背處行]
to cast aside, to throw away (Ming 棄了; reading uncertain) [棄了您]

sentences.l: Eyes' behind cast-away" said.
sentences.i: Put him out of our sight," he said.
sentences.n: nidün-ü ečine is 'behind the eyes' (Ming 眼的背處行): 'out of sight'. gedkün is read as a verb 'to cast aside' (Ming 棄了您), with -dkün, the imperative for 'you' plural (Ming 您); the published parts have gedkü- as a converb stem (Ming 撇), so the division is uncertain. The order is carried out in the next unit, which shows the sense is 'put to death'.

sentences.t: Tedüi-kü mököriġülbe.

morph.gloss: to cut, to behead (Ming 斬) [斬了]

sentences.l: Thereupon had-cut-down.
sentences.i: At once they had him beheaded.
sentences.n: tedüi-kü is 'thereupon, at once' (Ming 隨卽). mököriġülbe is a causative of a verb 'to cut, to behead' (Ming 斬了, 'cut down'): 'made (someone) cut off (his head)'. This ends §156.

sentences.t: Mün noγai žil Čiṅgis Qaγan-(n)i Tatar irgen-dür morilaγsan-dur

morph.gloss: the same, that very (Ming 只) [只]
Chinggis, the title borne by Temüjin from 1206 [太祖︀]

words.reading: 秣舌驪剌黑三-突︀舌兒 morilaγsan-dur

morph.gloss: verbal: to ride, to take the field
dative-locative: at, when (Ming 上馬了時)

sentences.l: Same dog year, Čiṅgis Qaγan, Tatar people-to, horse-mounting-when,
sentences.i: In that same Dog year, when Chinggis Qahan took the field against the Tatar people,
sentences.n: A § that begins, as the Ming does, with the year (mün noγai žil 'the same dog year'). I take Qaγan-(n)i as having the accusative or a reflexive ending (Ming 行), but the case is unclear to me. morilaγsan-dur is mori 'horse' with -la- 'to ride' and the participle -γsan with -dur 'at, when' (Ming 上馬了 時), 'when (one) had mounted', that is, taken the field.

sentences.t: Waṅ-Qān Merkid irgen-dür morilažu Toγtoγ̇a-Beki-ji Barγužin-Tögüm žüg hüldežü

morph.gloss: Wang Qan, the Kereid ruler (Ming 人名) [人名]
verbal: to ride, to take the field
Toqto'a Beki, a man's name (Ming 人名) [人名 行]

words.reading: 巴舌兒中忽眞-脫窟木 Barγužin-Tögüm

morph.gloss: Barqujin-Tögüm, a place (Ming 地名) [地名]

sentences.l: Waṅ-Qān, Merkid people-to, horse-mounting, Toγtoγ̇a-Beki-ACC Barγužin-Tögüm toward chasing,
sentences.i: Wang Qan rode against the Merkid people and chased Toqto'a Beki toward Barqujin Tögüm,
sentences.n: Waṅ-Qān is the Wang Qan of the earlier parts; the Ming has 人名. Merkid is a people (Ming 種(名)的). Toγtoγ̇a-Beki-ji takes the accusative (Ming 人名行); Barγužin-Tögüm is a place (Ming 地名), and the published parts have Barqujin and Tögüm as places; žüg is 'toward, in the direction' (Ming 往). hüldežü is hülde- 'to chase' (Ming 追着). The chain goes on for three more units; I cut it where the objects change.

sentences.t: Toγtoγ̇a-jin jeke köġün Tögüs- Beki-ji alažu

morph.gloss: Toqto'a, a man's name [人名 的]
Tögüs, a name (the Ming reads it with the next word) [人]
Beki, the second part of the name Tögüs-Beki [名 行]

sentences.l: Toγtoγ̇a's great son Tögüs-Beki-ACC killing,
sentences.i: killed Toqto'a's eldest son, Tögüs-Beki,
sentences.n: Toγtoγ̇a-jin is the genitive after a vowel. jeke köġün is 'great son' (Ming 大 子), which I take as 'eldest'. The name is printed Tögüs- / Beki-ji, split by the line (Ming 人 名行); Tögüs-Beki is one man; Beki, as in Toγtoγ̇a-Beki, may be a title, which the Ming (名) does not say. alažu is ala- 'to kill'.

sentences.t: Toγtoγ̇a-jin Quntuγtai, Čaγ̇arun žirin ökid in-ü qatud in-ü abču

morph.gloss: Toqto'a, a man's name [人名 的]
Quntuqtai, a woman's name (Ming 女名) [女名]
Cha'arun, a woman's name (Ming 女名) [女名]

sentences.l: Toγtoγ̇a's Quntuγtai, Čaγ̇arun two daughters his, ladies his, taking,
sentences.i: took Toqto'a's two daughters, Quntuqtai and Cha'arun, and his ladies,
sentences.n: žirin ökid is 'two daughters' (ökid is the plural of ökin; Ming 兩箇 女每); the two names are printed with Ming 女名. in-ü qatud in-ü abču is the puzzle. in-ü is placed after its noun elsewhere (an-u, namur in-ü), so I read 'ökid in-ü' as 'his daughters' and 'qatud in-ü' as 'his ladies' (Ming 娘子每 他的), the 'his' being Toqto'a, who is the only man named; the Wang Qan is the subject. The alternative, that the daughters were themselves taken as wives, would need the second in-ü to point to the Wang Qan and leaves the plural qatud unexplained; I leave it open.

sentences.t: Qutu, Čilaγ̇un qojar köġüd-i in-ü irge selte daγ̇uližu

morph.gloss: Qutu, a son's name (Ming 子名) [子名]
Chila'un, a son's name (Ming 子名) [子名]
people (variant of irgen; Ming 百姓) [百姓]
to plunder, to carry off [擄着]

sentences.l: Qutu, Čilaγ̇un two sons-ACC his, people together-with, plundering,
sentences.i: and carried off his two sons, Qutu and Chila'un, along with the people,
sentences.n: Qutu and Čilaγ̇un are 'son names' (Ming 子名); qojar köġüd-i is 'the two sons' (plural köġüd, accusative; Ming 兩箇 兒子每行). in-ü follows köġüd-i, 'his (Toqto'a's) sons', as in the previous unit; irge selte is 'with the people' (Ming 百姓 連; irge is a short form of irgen). The other division, in-ü irge 'his people', gives much the same sense. daγ̇uližu is the converb 'plundering' (Ming 擄着), so the units 'chasing, killing, taking, plundering' all belong to one chain that I cut up.

sentences.t: Čiṅgis Qaγ̇an-a jaγ̇u ber ese ögbe.

morph.gloss: Chinggis, the title borne by Temüjin from 1206 [太祖︀]
not (negates a past action; Ming 不曾) [不曾]

sentences.l: Čiṅgis Qaγan-to what even not gave.
sentences.i: and gave Chinggis Qahan nothing at all.
sentences.n: A short coda, and the one clause with a main verb that is not a converb. Qaγ̇an-a is 'to the Qahan' (Ming 皇帝 行). jaγ̇u ber 'what even' (Ming 甚麽 也), with ese 'not' (Ming 不曾), gives 'not anything at all'; ese is the negative of a past action, 'did not give' (Ming 與了, ögbe). The Mongol states no subject, and neither does the Ming; the Wang Qan, the subject of the chain, is the one who did not share with Chinggis.
